A group of randomly selected students from School A was asked about whether or not they use TV or the internet to access the local news. The results of the survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | TV | No TV | Totals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Internet | $90$ | $15$ | $105$ |
| No internet | $30$ | $15$ | $45$ |
| Totals | $120$ | $30$ | $150$ |

There are $100$ students in School B. Assuming that the distribution of the results is the same for both schools,
estimate the number of School B students that access the local news either from TV or the internet, but not both.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

A group of Lincoln High School students was randomly selected for a survey. They were asked about their preferences between the violin and the piano. The results of this survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Violin | Piano | Totals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Girls | $32$ | $10$ | $42$ |
| Boys | $18$ | $20$ | $38$ |
| Totals | $50$ | $30$ | $80$ |

There are $500$ students at JFK High School. Assuming the distribution of results is the same for both high schools, estimate the number of JFK High School students who are girls and like the violin.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Researchers surveyed students in School A on which superpower they would most like to have. The results of this survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Flying | Invisibility | Other | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Female | $16$ | $18$ | $12$ | $46$ |
| Male | $28$ | $12$ | $14$ | $54$ |
| Totals | $44$ | $30$ | $26$ | $100$ |

School B has $300$ students. Assuming the distribution of results is the same for both schools, estimate the number of School B students who are male and would choose to fly as their superpower.

A group of $5$th grade and $6$th grade students at Benjamin Franklin Elementary School are randomly selected for a survey. They are asked about their favorite places to go on summer vacations between the beach and the countryside. The results of this survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Beach | Countryside | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $5$th grade | $55$ | $30$ | $85$ |
| $6$th grade | $42$ | $33$ | $75$ |
| Totals | $97$ | $63$ | $160$ |

John Adams Elementary School has $250$ students in $5$th grade and $6$th grade. Assuming that the distribution of the results is the same in both elementary schools, estimate the number of students at John Adams Elementary School who are in $6$th grade or like to go to the beach on summer vacations (or both). Round your answer to the nearest integer.

A group of randomly selected students from Chicago High School was asked which country they want to visit between Brazil, Spain, France, or Japan. The results of the survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Brazil | Spain | France | Japan | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Girls | $12$ | $20$ | $9$ | $14$ | $55$ |
| Boys | $14$ | $10$ | $20$ | $1$ | $45$ |
| Totals | $26$ | $30$ | $29$ | $15$ | $100$ |

Boston High School has $400$ students. Assuming that the distribution of the results is the same in both high schools, estimate the number of girls at Boston High School who wish to visit Brazil or France. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
